goal: Every public page renders its brand suffix exactly once, and the 'Try the demo again' button on a failed onboarding demo produces a new demo instead of a 409.
non_goals: Do not take any item from #1078 section A — D9, D11, D33, S15 and X25 each need a product or schema decision and are separate feature runs.
Do not touch #1078 section D complexity hotspots; they are inherited from main and are separate refactor work.
Do not change the root layout's title template or its openGraph/twitter titles — the per-page openGraph gap is a different, pre-existing finding.
Do not add a retry cap or any new counter for failed demos; the existing cost reservation is the spend guard.
Do not change the demo status vocabulary or the archive-then-insert transaction shape.
Do not rename any page or change any visible page copy other than the browser title.
user_visible_behavior: The browser tab on /login, /signup, /signup/finish, /signup/check-email, /forgot-password, /reset-password, /features, /security, /u/[token] and the five /legal pages reads 'Name · RepWorth', not 'Name · RepWorth · RepWorth'.
The two legacy redirect stubs /privacy and /terms carry a bare title consistent with the rest, though their metadata never reaches a user.
An owner whose onboarding demo failed can press 'Try the demo again' and get a new demo, instead of a mapped 'no demo to regenerate' error every time.
invariants: The root layout stays the single owner of the ' · RepWorth' suffix (src/app/layout.tsx title.template).
Each edited page keeps its existing robots directive and every other metadata field unchanged.
The regenerate route stays a thin composition root: it parses, reserves budget, runs one transaction, returns — no business logic moves into it (invariant 12).
The regenerate route keeps its owner scoping by user_id AND business_id, and keeps its cost reservation and cleanup path.
The archive-then-insert stays in ONE transaction with its job_outbox row (invariant 2).
A demo in 'running', 'queued' or 'archived' status stays non-regenerable.
edge_cases: An owner with both a completed and a failed demo: ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1 still picks the most recent of the eligible set, so the newest failure wins over an older success.
An owner with no demo at all: still 409 no_demo_to_regenerate, and the client's existing mapped copy still applies.
A demo stuck in 'running': stays ineligible, so a retry cannot race the worker that is still generating it.
Redirect stub pages: their metadata never renders because permanentRedirect throws first; the title fix is for consistency, not for an observable change.
The /u/[token] page is a dynamic segment — its surface entry is the plain bracketed path, never pre-escaped (#867).
The title guard must read page files as text rather than importing them; importing a server component pulls next/font and the whole render path into the test.
existing_patterns_to_follow: src/app/(public)/how-it-works/page.tsx, pricing/page.tsx, book-a-demo/page.tsx and help/contact/page.tsx — already bare, with the comment naming the root template. Copy that comment convention.
src/app/onboarding/business/page.tsx — the A26 precedent this change extends to the remaining pages.
src/app/api/dashboard/__tests__/refusals-route.test.ts — the house route-test mocking level: mock @/lib/db/auth and @/lib/db/server, never the domain helpers.
src/app/(public)/help/contact/__tests__/ContactContent.test.tsx — an existing test that already asserts the bare-title convention.
test_seams: the exported metadata object of each edited page module
tests_to_add: no page metadata title under src/app spells the RepWorth brand suffix
the title guard names every offending file and its title when it fails
the regenerate route selects a demo whose generation_status is completed or failed
the regenerate route returns no_demo_to_regenerate when the owner has no completed or failed demo
the regenerate route does not select a demo whose generation_status is running, queued or archived
the regenerate route archives the selected failed demo and inserts its replacement in one transaction
rollback_plan: Revert the branch. No schema, no migration and no dependency changes; the title edits are metadata strings and the route edit is one WHERE predicate, so reverting restores today's behaviour exactly.
observability: The new title guard test is the regression signal — a future page that spells the suffix fails the gate rather than shipping a doubled title.
The existing onboarding demo analytics and the regenerate route's structured logs distinguish a successful retry from a 409, so the A14 fix is measurable after release.
